payload.body: A spectral-band feature is a quantitative descriptor computed from the per-bin energy values of a signal's power spectrum within a defined frequency sub-band [f_low, f_high), reducing the band-local energy vector to a scalar summary. The parameters are (1) the band bounds, (2) the underlying spectral decomposition, and (3) the specific scalar function applied (e.g., centroid, variance, flatness, flux). The construct persists as a standard computational routine implemented across audio analysis toolkits (Librosa, Essentia, HTK) and standardized in music information retrieval, speech processing, and acoustic monitoring systems. payload.body: Effective bandwidth is a scalar width descriptor of a signal's spectral (or line) energy distribution, defined as the width of the ideal rectangular pulse having the same peak height and the same total energy as the distribution. Parameters: (1) the per-bin energy values E_i (i = 1..N) of the spectral representation; (2) the per-bin frequency spacing delta_f. Computed as BW_eff = (sum(E_i) / max_i E_i) * delta_f: the dimensionless ratio of total energy to peak energy, scaled to frequency units (Hz). Unlike the centroid-spread bandwidth (the second central moment), it contains no centroid term: for a single-bin (pure-tone) distribution it yields delta_f, the width of one bin, and for a flat distribution over N bins it yields N * delta_f, the full occupied support. The persistence mechanism is standard arithmetic applied frame-by-frame to spectral decompositions in signal processing, spectroscopy, and RF and audio analysis, where it sizes the equivalent rectangular line width for filter and bandwidth budgeting. payload.body: Spectral-smoothness is a spectral analysis measure that quantifies how smoothly the per-bin energy values change across frequency in a full spectrum. It computes a weighted mean absolute derivative of adjacent bin energies, normalized by the spectrum's mean energy and the total number of bins, yielding a dimensionless index of spectral continuity. Parameters: (1) the spectral estimate (periodogram, Welch's method, or spectrogram slice), (2) the per-bin energy vector across all frequency bins. Computed as smoothness = 1 - (1/N) * Σ|E[i+1] - E[i]| / mean(E) where E[i] is the energy of bin i, N is the number of bins, and mean(E) is the arithmetic mean of all bin energies. Values range from 0 (highly irregular spectrum with abrupt energy changes) to approaching 1 (very smooth spectrum with gradual energy transitions). Displayed as a scalar time series over analysis frames. [formal: planities spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.30]

payload.body: Spectral-spread is a spectral analysis parameter quantifying the dispersion of spectral energy across the frequency bins of a full spectrum at a given analysis frame, unbounded by any sub-band. It is the square root of the spectrum's second central moment: the energy-weighted standard deviation of bin frequencies about the full-spectrum centroid. Parameters: (1) the full set of frequency bins i=1..N with center frequencies f_i, (2) the per-bin energy values E_i = |X[k_i]|^2 over the whole spectrum, (3) the analysis frame window. Computed as spread = sqrt( sum_i E_i * (f_i - c)^2 / sum_i E_i ), where c = sum_i(f_i * E_i) / sum_i(E_i) is the full-spectrum spectral-centroid. The value is in hertz: a large spread means energy is dispersed across the spectrum, a small spread means energy is concentrated near the centroid. It is the whole-spectrum counterpart of spectral-band-spread, which restricts the same formula to bins within [f_low, f_high). Persistence: the standardized mathematical definition of full-spectrum dispersion in spectral analysis, implemented in audio analysis toolkits and MIR feature pipelines. [formal: dispersio spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
